agent_flags.summary: freshness.py holds `time` as a module object so the perf test can intercept its clock, but freshness.time IS the singleton stdlib time module, so the patch replaces time.monotonic process-wide - including asyncio.BaseEventLoop.time(). Safe for this test (warm path does no I/O and schedules no timer; independently re-confirmed by the round-1 code review), but a future perf test doing awaited I/O under a timeout inside the patched window could hang or fire timers spuriously, and would look like a flaky perf test rather than a clock artifact. monkeypatch restores it in teardown, so there is no cross-test leak.
agent_flags.disposition: Accepted. Both the orchestrator and the round-1 code review independently confirmed the process-global time.monotonic patch is a non-defect for this specific test: the warm path performs no I/O and schedules no timer inside the patched window, and monkeypatch restores the original in teardown, so nothing leaks across tests. Not fixed because the alternatives (a _now() indirection in freshness.py, or an injectable clock alongside session_factory) both change frozen, gate-passed source for no present benefit. Kept open in the record as a constraint for the next author who reuses this seam - a future perf test doing awaited I/O under a timeout inside the patched window could hang, and would present as a flaky test rather than a clock artifact.

agent_flags.summary: The gate's specified consistency anchor - a hash of `git status --porcelain` - cannot detect content drift, because porcelain emits one status line per path and no content. Demonstrated: after an implementation-agent rewrote seven files (including app/services/freshness.py), the specified anchor returned the SAME hash, because the same paths still had the same statuses. The join guard therefore silently passes on the exact failure it exists to catch, and round 1's 'guard held' was true by construction rather than by evidence. Separately, the exclusion set (docs/features, docs/test-cases, docs/state) omits harness-written paths that change mid-gate: docs/activity/activity.jsonl is appended on agent completion (it alone tripped the corrected round-2 anchor), and a root-level .claude/agent-memory exclusion does not match the nested services/api/.claude/agent-memory this repo's validation-agent actually uses. Orchestrator mitigation: content-sensitive anchor (git diff HEAD + per-file shasum over untracked source) with the full exclusion set, corroborated by an mtime-vs-dispatch check that names the drifting file instead of only reporting that a hash moved. Affects every story's gate.
agent_flags.disposition: Accepted as out of BED-04's scope, with the mitigation retained in this story's record. The defect is in .claude/skills/arh-implement/steps/02-validate.md, not in BED-04: a status-based anchor cannot detect content drift, and the exclusion set omits docs/activity/ and nested */.claude/agent-memory/. Both halves were demonstrated concretely this session rather than argued in principle - the specified anchor returned an identical hash after seven files were rewritten, and the corrected content-sensitive anchor was tripped solely by an activity-log append. The orchestrator ran the gate on a corrected anchor plus an mtime-vs-dispatch cross-check, so BED-04's own round-2 GREEN was earned against a source tree proven stable. Fixing the skill would change every story's gate and belongs in harness work.
